13 / 21 · Change

Ordered graph diffs

A graph patch describes a transition between two versions. Its edits contain before and after values, and its cause points to the inputs that produced the change.

Contract illustration
InputProjectionDiff
◉ Active+ Added− RemovedΔ Changed× Rejected
The rule
What the contract requires
An input that leaves graph state unchanged emits no graph patch. Acceptance, progress and telemetry remain separate.
The boundary
Scope and constraints
Batching keeps constituent patches and their revision boundaries. Squashing is a distinct operation that can discard intermediate history.
Example · C#
Batch and compose ordered patches
Full source ↗
A batch keeps event boundaries. Ordered composition checks adjacent revisions.
UsageExamples.cs
public static PatchBatch PreserveEventBoundaries(GraphPatch first, GraphPatch next) =>
    new([first, next]);

public static EvaluatePatch ComposePatches(GraphPatch first, GraphPatch next) =>
    new(new RequestId("compose"),
        new PatchThen(new PatchLiteral(first), new PatchLiteral(next)));
// Composition requires first.To == next.From and compatible graph scope.
// The algebra validates before-states; construction alone does not apply edits.
Compile-checked caller example. Execution requires implementations of the injected interfaces.
